 ORDER Accused in Spl.C.No:255/2023 pending before the Court of Additional District & Sessions Judge,
FTSC-I, Davanagere for the offences punishable Under Sections 363, 366(A) and 376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ('the IPC' for short), Section 6 of the POCSO Act and Section 9 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, is before this Court seeking regular bail.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and learned HCGP appearing for respondent No. 1.

3. On the basis of the complaint lodged by the Smt. Shanthamma dated 07.12.2022, Davanagere Women Police Station had initially registered a FIR in crime No.161/2022 for the offences punishable Under Section 363 of the IPC against unknown persons.
In the complaint, it is averred that the NC: 2023:KHC:29292 complainant's daughter who was studying Ist PUC was found missing from the house on 03.12.2022.

entities.text: NC: 2023:KHC:29292 complainant's daughter who was studying Ist PUC
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Thereafter, the complainant and her family members had searched for the missing minor girl.
Since her whereabouts were not known, on 07.12.2022 the complainant had approached the Police and lodged the complaint, which had resulted in registering FIR in crime No.161/2022.

During the course of the investigation the victim girl was traced along with the petitioner on 04.01.2023, the victim girl was brought back home and the petitioner was arrested and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is complete and the charge sheet has been filed on 16.02.2023 against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
His bail application filed before the trial Court in Spl.C.No.255/2023 was dismissed on 20.04.2023.
It is under these circumstances, the petitioner is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has reiterated the grounds urged in the petition and submits that the victim girl had voluntarily accompanied the petitioner.

He also submits that in her Sri. Aruna K.N vs State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82367708/
2 statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., the victim girl has not made any allegations against NC: 2023:KHC:29292 the petitioner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also submits that the medical report of the victim girl does not support the case of the prosecution.

The investigation is complete and charge sheet has been filed and hence, he prays to allow the petition.
5.

Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the bail application contending that the victim girl is a minor and there are serious allegations of sexual assault and therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.
6. On the basis of the complaint lodged by the victim girl initially a case was registered against unknown persons for the offence punishable under Section 363 of the IPC.
During the course of the investigation, the victim girl was traced along with the petitioner in his aunt's house.

Thereafter,
they were brought back and the statement of victim girl under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. was recorded before the Jurisdictional Magistrate on 09.01.2023.
In her statement, the victim girl has stated that she was in love with petitioner for the last two years.
Her parents intended to marry her to some other person, but she had opposed the same, however, they were not listening.

Therefore,
on 03.12.2022 she had called the NC: 2023:KHC:29292 petitioner and asked him to take her to a distant place.
She has stated that she had voluntarily gone with the petitioner to Kadur and thereafter to Sakarepatana and had got married in a temple.
For a period of 15 days they were staying at Birur in a house and thereafter they came to Kundur village and stayed in the house of the petitioner's aunt.
From the said house, the Police had brought her back.
7. From the reading of the statement of the victim girl under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., it is seen that there is no allegations of sexual assault made on her by the petitioner.
The medical report of the victim girl would go to show that external injuries were not found on the body of the victim girl.
The petitioner, who is aged about 21 years is in custody since 04.01.2023.
Investigation in the case is complete and the charge sheet has been filed.
His custody is not required by the prosecution for any purpose.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted the petitioner has no criminal antecedents and his submission is not seriously disputed by the learned HCGP.
Under these circumstances, I am of the view that the petitioner has made out a prime facie case for grant of regular bail.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.161/2022 of Davangere Women Police Station registered for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366(A) and 376 of the IPC,
subject to the following conditions:
a) Petitioner shall execute personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000 (Rupees One Lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum, to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court;
